content.text:
I've built `spec.vl.json`. It renders with no errors or warnings, and all 263,088 rows are loaded straight from the URL. The default render checks out. I couldn't test dragging or clicking in the render tool, so the brush interaction itself is untested.

The figure has three stacked panels:
- **Overview:** daily mean temperature with a daily min–max band, 2020–2024. You drag a range on it to pick the period.
- **Temperature detail:** every 10-minute reading in the chosen period, as a line with a point per reading.
- **Precipitation detail:** 10-minute rainfall as bars, on the same UTC time axis as the temperature detail.

It opens on an arbitrary week, 8–15 July 2024. To check the caption, I downloaded a copy of the CSV to `/tmp` and looked at it; the deliverable doesn't use that copy. That check shows yearly maxima of 35.0–36.7 °C and no empty fields.

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - daily mean line plus daily min–max band for tl, 2020–2024, aggregated inside the spec
  R2: done - detail shows raw 10-min tl readings (line plus a point per reading) for the brushed period
  R3: done - interval brush on the overview filters the detail and sets its x domain
  R4: done - separate rr bar track (each bar spans its 10-min interval), sharing the detail's UTC x domain
  R5: done - overview ticks "Mon YYYY" every 6 months; detail uses Vega's automatic multi-scale UTC labels (days/hours/minutes)
  R6: done - full CSV loaded from the URL; aggregation only in Vega-Lite transforms
  R7: done - axes show °C, mm per 10 min and UTC; title plus a one-sentence caption in the subtitle
assumptions:
  - Opening brush set to 8–15 July 2024 (an arbitrary week) so the detail is never empty or overloaded at load; it is not chosen from data values
  - Each rr value is taken to cover the 10 minutes ending at its time stamp
  - Overview aggregates to UTC calendar days (mean/min/max)
  - The caption text is written by hand from the overview pattern; the maxima were checked against the data (35.0–36.7 °C per year)
limitations:
  - Clearing the brush (click outside it) shows all 263k readings in the detail, which is slow and unreadable
  - The detail can't be zoomed or panned by itself; the period is set only through the overview brush
  - Precipitation bars are very thin for periods longer than a few days
  - Missing values (none found) would be dropped by the filters, so the line would bridge any gap
  - Brush dragging and clicking was not tested; only the static default render was checked
```
